beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Makers of Reality explores a world where money no longer organizes access.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its novel begins with needed goods immobilized by incompatible valid instructions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Later abundance changes the problem without removing decisions about allocation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel examines how power changes when prices disappear.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows material needs into the less visible rules governing their satisfaction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Abundance supplies possibilities while leaving disagreement about their consequences intact.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The opening shipment contains filters that hospitals need to receive.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its governing instructions can each be valid while remaining impossible to satisfy together.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The drone obeys them all by staying where it is.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That impasse makes coordination a visible problem before the economic order changes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Money is part of the story, but it is not its only organizing device.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel asks what happens when access and authority must be described differently.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Later, ordinary goods can be obtained without the familiar act of purchasing them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their availability does not erase water, effort, attention, or conflicting priorities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Allocation makes those consequences objects of interpretation and public argument.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The story follows people who describe needs and others who question the descriptions.
